newsitem.title: UK: CCN survey warns of fragility of UK economy.
newsitem.headline: CCN survey warns of fragility of UK economy.

text.p: Britain's economy is on a knife-edge even though company profitability at the end of last year was at its highest level for five years, business information group CCN said.
Its latest "Corporate Health Check" showed the return on capital achieved by British companies was 12.43 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"On the surface, the economy appears to be the healthiest it's been for several years," said CCN director David Coates.

"Manufacturing output is buoyant, if somewhat erratic, housing starts increased strongly in the second half of last year, new mortgage advances were well ahead of the previous year, which fed through to increased demand for large ticket household goods, and factory gate inflation is the lowest for 10 years."

But on the other hand, the strength of the pound, the prospects of a post-election interest rate rise, skill shortages in key areas and continuing weak capital investment could come together to reverse the recovery of the last three years.
"The economy is on a knife edge and the wrong policies over the next year could undo all the hard work of the last three years," CCN said.
Coates said the economy was the strongest it had been since the end of the recession but manufacturing industry was having to run fast just to stand still.
The next government needed to take action to stimulate investment and training to prevent consumer and industrial demand being met by increased imports.

"The stop-go nature of UK industrial performance is causing long-term structural weaknesses among many industrial sectors, with short-term considerations taking priority over long term strategies for investment and growth," Coates added.
